## formal
Read numbers in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$. Let $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ be the composite space of Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}(a) with fermionic slot module $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, $D$ the slot doublet; let $a_{i} = a(u_{i}) \otimes 1$ ($i = 1, 2$) be the slot annihilators, $b_{p} = 1 \otimes b(t_{p})$ ($p = 1, 2, 3$) the pair annihilators, $(-1)^{k}$ the pair parity, $(-1)^{N} = (-1)^{n + k}$ the grading, and $\tilde a_{i} = a_{i}(-1)^{k}$ the Klein-twisted slot operators.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Same slot data; proved.)} The $\tilde a_{i}$ satisfy the same canonical anticommutation relations as the $a_{i}$, transform in the same way under $U(2) \times U(3)$, and on $F_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ have $\tilde a_{i}^{\dagger} = (-1)^{k}a_{i}^{\dagger}$, so clause (G) holds for one set exactly when it holds for the other.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Opposite relation to the pairs; proved.)} The $a_{i}$ commute with every $b_{p}$, $b_{p}^{\dagger}$; the $\tilde a_{i}$ anticommute with them. So $\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}, b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes, and their real Majorana combinations, five of square $+1$ and five of square $-1$, generate $\Cl(5,5)$ on $V$, whose span over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ is the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Convention-free operators; proved.)} The $21$ split-preserving bivectors (the $6$ slot-slot and $15$ pair-pair Majorana bivectors, the Pati-Salam algebra of clause (CPT)) and the grading $(-1)^{N}$, which anticommutes with $a_{i}$, $\tilde a_{i}$ and $b_{p}$ alike, are the same operators in both conventions.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Uniqueness; proved.)} If an operator $K$ on $V$ commutes with every $a_{i}$, $a_{i}^{\dagger}$ and the $a_{i}K$ anticommute with every pair operator and satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations, then $K = c(-1)^{k}$ with $c$ a unit of $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ (a phase from the centre of the slot $U(2)$), and $c = \pm 1$ if $K$ is an involution.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Consequence; proved on $V$.)} Clause (f) holds on $V$ for every $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, canonically up to that unit: it is a convention on $V$, and the qualifier of clause (CPT) ``when the slot module is fermionic, so that clause (f) applies'' adds no condition beyond $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}D$. The clause keeps content only relative to slot operators given in advance, for instance as tower elements (the setting of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}(iii)), which is not addressed.
\end{enumerate}
In the floor $\Cl(5,5)$ of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}, with the modes as null pairs of vectors, the twisted operators are the vectors themselves, the untwisted ones are the vectors times the pair parity $\Gamma_{W} = e_{2}f_{2}e_{3}f_{3}e_{4}f_{4}$, a single blade, and (iv) is a count of blades with the commutation form of \claimref{synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form}(ii). Transport-absent.

## technical
Clause (f) of the slot-module hypothesis asks that the slot and pair operators of a composite form one system of five fermionic modes, each slot operator anticommuting with each pair operator. On the tensor-product space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ the natural slot operators commute with the pair operators instead. Multiplying them by the pair parity $(-1)^{k}$, the Klein transformation, turns commuting into anticommuting while keeping their anticommutation relations, their $U(2) \times U(3)$ behaviour and their images, so generation is unaffected. Everything the hypothesis asks of the chirality is the same in both conventions: the slot-slot and pair-pair bivectors (the Pati-Salam algebra) and the grading by the total mode number. The twist is unique: a factor commuting with the slot operators and making them anticommute with the pairs is a unit times $(-1)^{k}$, because it then commutes with all operators on $V$. In geometric algebra the five modes are null pairs of vectors in $\Cl(5,5)$, the twisted slot operators are those vectors, and the pair parity is the single blade $e_{2}f_{2}e_{3}f_{3}e_{4}f_{4}$; uniqueness is then a count with the two-element-field commutation form of blades. So on $V$ clause (f) is a convention, not a premise; it would carry content only for slot operators fixed in advance, for instance as tower elements, which this result does not treat. Transport-absent.

## lay
The series builds each quark or lepton from two kinds of ingredients, slots and pairs, and one of its assumptions says that the two kinds behave as a single family of fermions, swapping sign whenever one of each is exchanged. This result shows that, on the particle's own space of states, this costs nothing: if slot and pair operators are first written so that they ignore each other, a standard trick (multiplying each slot operator by a sign that counts the pairs) makes them behave as one family, changes nothing else that the theory uses, and is the only way to do it up to an overall sign. The assumption only matters if the slot operators are fixed in advance by something else, such as the deeper tower of the theory.

## one-liner
On the composite space $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}D \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ the Klein-twisted slot operators $a(-1)^{k}$ keep the slot CAR, covariance and generation, anticommute with the pair operators where the untwisted ones commute, leave the $21$ Pati-Salam bivectors and the grading unchanged, and are unique up to a unit, so clause (f) is a convention on $V$, with content only for slot operators fixed in advance.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Notation.} Numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ (conventions); $D$ is the slot doublet, $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$; $a_{i} = a(u_{i}) \otimes 1$ ($u_{1}, u_{2}$ an orthonormal basis of $D$, $a^{\dagger}(u) = u \wedge$), $b_{p} = 1 \otimes b(t_{p})$ ($t_{1}, t_{2}, t_{3}$ an orthonormal basis of $W$), $(-1)^{k} = 1 \otimes (-1)^{\deg}$ the pair parity, $(-1)^{N} = (-1)^{n}(-1)^{k}$, and $\tilde a_{i} = a_{i}(-1)^{k}$. Products of operators on a tensor product: $(X \otimes Y)(X' \otimes Y') = XX' \otimes YY'$, so operators on different factors commute.

\emph{Step 1 (realisation in geometric algebra).} Take the floor $\Cl(5,5)$ of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}: generators $e_{k}$ ($e_{k}^{2} = 1$), $f_{k}$ ($f_{k}^{2} = -1$), $k = 0, \dots, 4$, null pairs $v_{k} = \tfrac12(e_{k} + f_{k})$, $w_{k} = \tfrac12(e_{k} - f_{k})$ with $v_{k}w_{l} + w_{l}v_{k} = \delta_{kl}$ and all other anticommutators zero, modes $0, 1$ the slots and $2, 3, 4$ the pairs, vacuum the null blade $\Omega = w_{0}\cdots w_{4}$. The $32$ states $v_{K}v_{J}\Omega$ ($v_{K}$ an ordered product of pair creators, $v_{J}$ of slot creators) are independent and span the Fock ideal; identify $v_{K}v_{J}\Omega$ with $u_{J} \otimes t_{K}$. A pair vector, acting from the left, passes no slot vector, so it acts as $1 \otimes b$; a slot vector passes the $k$ pair creators of $v_{K}$, so it acts as $a \otimes (-1)^{k}$: the vectors $v_{i}, w_{i}$ ($i = 0, 1$) are the twisted $\tilde a^{\dagger}_{i}, \tilde a_{i}$, and the untwisted ones are $v_{i}\Gamma_{W}$, $w_{i}\Gamma_{W}$ with $\Gamma_{W} = \prod_{p}(1 - 2v_{p}w_{p})$, the pair parity, as in clause (iii) of that result. Since $2v_{p}w_{p} = \tfrac12(e_{p} + f_{p})(e_{p} - f_{p}) = 1 - e_{p}f_{p}$, $1 - 2v_{p}w_{p} = e_{p}f_{p}$ and $\Gamma_{W} = e_{2}f_{2}e_{3}f_{3}e_{4}f_{4}$ is a single blade, $\Gamma_{W}^{2} = 1$, commuting with the slot vectors and anticommuting with the six pair vectors. Over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, $I_{4}$ commuting with all ten generators, $\Cl(5,5)$ spans $\mathrm{End}(V)$.

\emph{Step 2 ((i) and (ii)).} $\Gamma_{W}$ commutes with $a_{i}$, $a_{i}^{\dagger}$ and squares to $1$, so $\tilde a_{i}\tilde a_{j}^{\dagger} + \tilde a_{j}^{\dagger}\tilde a_{i} = a_{i}a_{j}^{\dagger} + a_{j}^{\dagger}a_{i} = \delta_{ij}$ and likewise for the other anticommutators. $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}B$ preserves the pair degree, so it commutes with $(-1)^{k}$ and $\tilde a_{i}$ transforms as $a_{i}$ does. On $F_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$, $\tilde a_{i}^{\dagger} = (-1)^{k}a_{i}^{\dagger}$, so the creation maps have the same images and clause (G) holds for one set exactly when it holds for the other. The $a_{i}$ act on the first factor and the $b_{p}$ on the second, so they commute; $(-1)^{k}$ anticommutes with $b_{p}$ and $b_{p}^{\dagger}$, so $\tilde a_{i}b_{p} = -b_{p}\tilde a_{i}$ (in $\Cl(5,5)$: distinct vectors anticommute). Hence $\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}, b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes, and the real Majorana combinations $\tilde a + \tilde a^{\dagger}$, $\tilde a - \tilde a^{\dagger}$, $b + b^{\dagger}$, $b - b^{\dagger}$ are the ten vectors $e_{k}$, $f_{k}$, generating $\Cl(5,5)$; its span over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ is the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f), with no imaginary unit needed for the Majorana of square $-1$.

\emph{Step 3 ((iii)).} For two slot operators $x, y$, $(x\Gamma_{W})(y\Gamma_{W}) = xy\,\Gamma_{W}^{2} = xy$; so every slot-slot bilinear, in particular the $\binom{4}{2} = 6$ slot Majorana bivectors, is the same element in both conventions. The pair operators are not twisted, so the $\binom{6}{2} = 15$ pair Majorana bivectors are the same too: the $21$ split-preserving bivectors of clause (CPT), the Pati-Salam algebra (\claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}, cited for the name only), do not depend on the convention. $\Gamma_{W}$ commutes with every slot-slot and pair-pair bilinear, the generators of $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$ and the pair creation and annihilation bilinears among them. The grading $(-1)^{N} = \prod_{k=0}^{4}e_{k}f_{k}$ anticommutes with every one of the ten vectors and commutes with $\Gamma_{W}$, so it anticommutes with $a_{i}$, $\tilde a_{i}$ and $b_{p}$ alike: the grading form of clause (CPT) does not depend on the convention either.

\emph{Step 4 ((iv), uniqueness).} Let $K$ commute with every $a_{i}$, $a_{i}^{\dagger}$, and let $a_{i}K$ anticommute with every $b_{p}$, $b_{p}^{\dagger}$ and satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations. For a pair operator $\beta$, $a_{i}K\beta + \beta a_{i}K = a_{i}(K\beta + \beta K)$, and likewise with $a_{i}^{\dagger}$; adding $a_{i}^{\dagger}$ times the first to $a_{i}$ times the second gives $K\beta + \beta K = 0$. So $K(-1)^{k}$ commutes with every pair operator and every slot operator. The slot operators generate $\mathrm{End}(F) \otimes 1$ and the pair operators $1 \otimes \mathrm{End}(\Lambda^{\bullet}W)$ (the Fock representations of the canonical anticommutation relations are irreducible), which together generate $\mathrm{End}(V)$; so $K(-1)^{k}$ is a number $c \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, and the relation $(a_{i}K)(a_{i}K)^{\dagger} + (a_{i}K)^{\dagger}(a_{i}K) = |c|^{2} = 1$ makes $c$ a unit; $c = \pm 1$ when $K$ is an involution or a real element of the floor. A unit $c$ is a phase that the centre of the slot $U(2)$ already supplies. In the realisation the same follows by counting blades with the commutation form of \claimref{synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form}(ii): blades $e_{S}$, $e_{T}$ anticommute exactly when $b(S, T) = |S||T| + |S \cap T| = 1 \pmod 2$; the conditions are diagonal in the blade basis, and with $P = \{e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{4}, f_{2}, f_{3}, f_{4}\}$, $b(S, \{x\}) = |S| + [x \in S] = 1$ for all $x \in P$ forces $S \supseteq P$ with $|S|$ even or $S \cap P = \emptyset$ with $|S|$ odd, and commuting with the untwisted slot Majoranas $e_{S'}$, $S' = \{y\} \cup P$, forces $[y \in S] = |S| + |S \cap P| \pmod 2$ for the four slot generators $y$; the first case gives $S = P$, the second would need all four slot generators in $S$ with $|S| = 4$ odd. So $K \in \mathrm{span}\{\Gamma_{W}\}$.

\emph{Step 5 (the reading; (v)).} By Steps 2 to 4, on $V$ the operators required by clause (f) exist whenever $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, namely the Klein-twisted slot operators, unique up to a unit; every operator the clause produces ($\Cl(10)$, $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, the $24$ cross bivectors) is an operator on $V$ built from them, and everything clause (CPT) asks of the convention is convention-free. So on $V$ clause (f) is a choice of convention with no content of its own. It keeps content only relative to an embedding of slot operators given in advance, for instance as tower elements, where the question is whether the given operators are the twisted or the untwisted ones; this is the setting of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}(iii), which already makes the replacement $s_{i} \mapsto s_{i}\Gamma_{W}$, and it is not addressed here. The checks verify Steps 1 to 4 exactly in $\Cl(5,5)$, including the commutation form against the products for all $1024$ blades.

check_py:
"""Clause (f) of the slot-module hypothesis is a Klein convention on V: exact checks in Cl(5,5).

Realisation (the floor of synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator): generators e_0..e_4 (square +1) and
f_0..f_4 (square -1), null pairs v_k = (e_k + f_k)/2, w_k = (e_k - f_k)/2 (v w + w v = 1 as vectors); modes 0, 1
are the slots, 2, 3, 4 the pairs; vacuum f = w_0 ... w_4; V is spanned by the 32 states x_K x_J f (pair
creators x_K to the left of slot creators x_J), so the pair vectors act as 1 (x) b and the slot vectors as the
Klein-twisted a (x) (-1)^k. Gamma_W = prod_p (1 - 2 v_p w_p) is the pair parity (-1)^k; the untwisted
(tensor-product) slot operators are v_i Gamma_W, w_i Gamma_W.

(1) Both conventions satisfy the slot CAR; the untwisted ones commute with every pair vector, the twisted ones
    (the vectors) anticommute; on the Fock basis they differ by the sign (-1)^k only (generation unchanged).
(2) Gamma_W = e_2 f_2 e_3 f_3 e_4 f_4 (one blade, 1 - 2 v w = e f); it commutes with every slot-slot and every
    pair-pair bilinear (so both conventions are covariant in the same way); the 6 slot-slot and 15 pair-pair
    Majorana bivectors (21) are the same elements in both conventions; the grading prod_k (1 - 2 v_k w_k)
    anticommutes with all ten twisted Majoranas and with the four untwisted slot Majoranas.
(3) Uniqueness: with the commutation form b(S, T) = |S||T| + |S cap T| mod 2 of
    synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form (checked against the products), the only blade anticommuting
    with the six pair Majoranas and commuting with the four untwisted slot Majoranas is that of Gamma_W; so a
    twist K commuting with the slot operators and making them anticommute with the pairs is c Gamma_W, and the
    CAR hold for a_i K exactly when c^2 = 1 (c = 1, -1 pass, c = 2 fails).
Exact arithmetic only.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations
import GA
from tp_premise import premise

NM = 5
SQ = tuple([1] * NM + [-1] * NM)
EG = [GA.gen(k) for k in range(NM)]
FG = [GA.gen(NM + k) for k in range(NM)]
V = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(EG[k], FG[k])) for k in range(NM)]
W = [GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.sub(EG[k], FG[k])) for k in range(NM)]
SLOTS = [0, 1]
PAIRS = [2, 3, 4]


def _m(*xs):
    r = GA.sc(1)
    for x in xs:
        r = GA.mul(r, x, SQ)
    return r


def _parity(modes):
    g = GA.sc(1)
    for k in modes:
        g = _m(g, GA.sub(GA.sc(1), GA.scal(F(2), _m(V[k], W[k]))))
    return g


GW = _parity(PAIRS)
GTOT = _parity(range(NM))
VAC = _m(*W)


def _states():
    out = []
    for kk in range(len(PAIRS) + 1):
        for K in combinations(PAIRS, kk):
            for jj in range(len(SLOTS) + 1):
                for J in combinations(SLOTS, jj):
                    out.append((len(K), _m(*([V[p] for p in K] + [V[i] for i in J] + [VAC]))))
    return out


def _acomm(x, y):
    return GA.add(_m(x, y), _m(y, x))


def _comm(x, y):
    return GA.sub(_m(x, y), _m(y, x))


def check_both_slot_conventions_obey_the_car_and_differ_by_the_pair_parity():
    premise("synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator")
    tw = [(V[i], W[i]) for i in SLOTS]
    un = [(_m(V[i], GW), _m(W[i], GW)) for i in SLOTS]
    pair_ops = [V[p] for p in PAIRS] + [W[p] for p in PAIRS]
    ok_car = True
    for ops in (tw, un):
        for i in range(2):
            for j in range(2):
                ok_car = ok_car and GA.eq(_acomm(ops[i][0], ops[j][1]), GA.sc(1 if i == j else 0))
                ok_car = ok_car and GA.is_zero(_acomm(ops[i][0], ops[j][0]))
                ok_car = ok_car and GA.is_zero(_acomm(ops[i][1], ops[j][1]))
    GA.check("(1) both conventions satisfy the slot CAR", ok_car)
    GA.check("(1) untwisted slot operators commute with every pair operator",
             all(GA.is_zero(_comm(x, y)) for pr in un for x in pr for y in pair_ops))
    GA.check("(1) twisted slot operators anticommute with every pair operator",
             all(GA.is_zero(_acomm(x, y)) for pr in tw for x in pr for y in pair_ops))
    sts = _states()
    GA.check("(1) the 32 Fock states are independent",
             len(sts) == 32 and GA.rank_of_vectors([[s.get(b, F(0)) for b in GA.all_blades(10)] for _, s in sts]) == 32)
    ok_sign = True
    for k, s in sts:
        for i in range(2):
            for x, y in zip(tw[i], un[i]):
                ok_sign = ok_sign and GA.eq(_m(y, s), GA.scal(F((-1) ** k), _m(x, s)))
    GA.check("(1) on the Fock basis the two conventions differ by (-1)^k (same images: generation kept)", ok_sign)


def check_split_preserving_bivectors_and_grading_are_convention_free():
    premise("synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator")
    blade = _m(EG[2], FG[2], EG[3], FG[3], EG[4], FG[4])
    GA.check("(2) Gamma_W is the blade e2 f2 e3 f3 e4 f4 and squares to 1",
             GA.eq(GW, blade) and GA.eq(_m(GW, GW), GA.sc(1)))
    bil = [_m(x, y) for a in SLOTS for b in SLOTS for x in (V[a], W[a]) for y in (V[b], W[b])]
    bil += [_m(x, y) for a in PAIRS for b in PAIRS for x in (V[a], W[a]) for y in (V[b], W[b])]
    GA.check("(2) Gamma_W commutes with every slot-slot and pair-pair bilinear",
             all(GA.is_zero(_comm(GW, x)) for x in bil))
    smaj = [EG[i] for i in SLOTS] + [FG[i] for i in SLOTS]
    pmaj = [EG[p] for p in PAIRS] + [FG[p] for p in PAIRS]
    smaj_un = [_m(x, GW) for x in smaj]
    same = [GA.eq(_m(smaj[a], smaj[b]), _m(smaj_un[a], smaj_un[b])) for a, b in combinations(range(4), 2)]
    GA.check("(2) the 6 slot-slot Majorana bivectors agree in both conventions", len(same) == 6 and all(same))
    GA.check("(2) 6 + 15 = 21 split-preserving bivectors",
             len(same) + len(list(combinations(pmaj, 2))) == 21)
    GA.check("(2) the grading anticommutes with all ten twisted Majoranas",
             all(GA.is_zero(_acomm(GTOT, x)) for x in smaj + pmaj))
    GA.check("(2) and with the four untwisted slot Majoranas",
             all(GA.is_zero(_acomm(GTOT, x)) for x in smaj_un))


def _bform(S, T):
    return (len(S) * len(T) + len(set(S) & set(T))) % 2


def check_the_klein_twist_is_unique_up_to_sign():
    premise("synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form")
    P = (2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9)
    pair_gens = [(p,) for p in P]
    slot_un = [tuple(sorted((i,) + P)) for i in (0, 1, 5, 6)]
    ok_form = True
    for S in GA.all_blades(10):
        for T in pair_gens + slot_un:
            anti = GA.anticommutes({S: F(1)}, {T: F(1)}, SQ)
            ok_form = ok_form and (anti == (_bform(S, T) == 1))
    GA.check("(3) b(S, T) = 1 exactly when the blades anticommute (10 generator blades, all S)", ok_form)
    sols = [S for S in GA.all_blades(10)
            if all(_bform(S, T) == 1 for T in pair_gens) and all(_bform(S, T) == 0 for T in slot_un)]
    GA.check("(3) the only such blade is the pair blade P (Gamma_W)", sols == [P])
    car = {}
    for c in (1, -1, 2):
        K = GA.scal(F(c), GW)
        a, ad = _m(W[0], GW, K), _m(V[0], GW, K)
        car[c] = GA.eq(_acomm(a, ad), GA.sc(1))
    GA.check("(3) a_i (c Gamma_W) satisfy the CAR exactly for c^2 = 1", car == {1: True, -1: True, 2: False})
